payload.big_idea: INHERITED from se.vision by pointer, no deviation. Delta for this iteration, one breath: the record of how a decision was reached stops cluttering the place where the decisions live. Lineage: se-v2-design §4 ("main holds live claims; branches hold the record of how they got there"), reached here through note-989ab09c39b0 and the i8c ship that produced no commit.
payload.to_be_world: An iteration opens in its own tree and commits as it goes, so its work is durable from the first milestone rather than only at the end. When it closes, trunk gains exactly what future iterations must read - the design nodes, the requirements, the tests, the product - and nothing else. The evidence, the gate records and the dead machine state do not vanish; they stay one tag away, named and reachable forever. Someone opening the repo a year later sees a clean set of live claims, and can still ask any shipped iteration exactly how it got there.
payload.goal_system: Primary: trunk carries only live claims. Second: nothing is ever lost - every event stays reachable by a named handle, which is why the tag is mandatory rather than polite. Third: work is durable mid-iteration, not only at the close. CONFLICT NAMED: the primary goal fights auditability - once evidence leaves trunk, a cross-iteration audit over gate contents means walking N tags instead of one query. The design accepts that cost explicitly, and the owner ruled today that the thin grant index stays on trunk to buy most of it back, on the condition that it stays an index and never grows content. Priority when they collide: nothing-lost outranks trunk-cleanliness - if a merge cannot prove the events remain reachable, it must refuse rather than proceed.
payload.moore_pitch: FOR the engineer running iterations in this repo, WHO needs the ledger to stay readable while the record stays complete, THE close-and-merge split IS a git mechanic that separates live claims from events at the moment an iteration closes, UNLIKE today's all-or-nothing merge, which either drags every evidence file onto trunk or - as i8c proved - merges nothing at all. THE DIFFERENCE is that the merge commit keeps both parents while its tree keeps only the claims, so the record is one tag away instead of underfoot.
